newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca sees 1996 profits in line with mkt.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca sees 1996 profits in line with mkt.

text.p: Zeneca Group Plc said on Tuesday that it expected its 1996 pre-tax profit to be in line with market expectations.
Zeneca announces its full-year results on March 11.
The company also said sales of new pharmaceutical products last year, particualrly of Casodex and Arimidex, "exceeded expectations".

The company said in a statement that pharmaceuticals profits for the year "are expected to show a growth rate slightly higher than that reported in 1995", while agro-chemical profit growth "although high" is expected to be slower than in 1995.

Zeneca said "strong volume growth" in pharmaceuticals helped to achieve an underlying annual sales rise "comparable" to the 14 percent growth seen at the nine-month stage, adding that pricing pressures had a "marginal" impact overall.

The group's biggest-selling product, cardiovascular treatment Zestril, saw full-year sales growth at similar levels to 1995, when they rose by 12 percent. Sales of prostate cancer treatment Zoladex "continued to grow strongly," while the first-half decline in sales of the breast cancer product Nolvadex slowed.
Sales of agro-chemicals were close to the 14 percent rise reported at the nine-month stage, the company said, with record sales of herbicides and of the insecticide Karate.
Operating profits at the slimmed-down specialties business are likely to be above 1995 levels after "a particularly strong second-half performance", the company added.

Full-year results will be affected by a 35 million stg reorganisation charge on specialty disposals, signalled at the half-year stage, while reoganisation of the seeds joint venture should cost Zeneca around 20 million stg.
